title: Kunneth formula, etale cohomology
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed
field and let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes of finite type over $k$.
Let $n\ge1$ be an integer invertible in $k$. Then for
$E\in D(X_{\Et},\kunZn)$ and $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\kunZn)$ the
Kunneth map of [def-kun-kunneth-map]

$$
\kappa_{E,K}:\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\kunZn}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)
\longrightarrow
\RGamma\bigl((X\times_kY)_{\Et},
\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism. (*Source:* Stacks Project, Tag
[0F1P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1P).)

proof.text:
Write $a:X\to\Spec(k)$ and $b:Y\to\Spec(k)$ for the structure morphisms. Apply [lem-kun-0f1n] with $S'=\Spec(k)$, $T=Y$, $p=\operatorname{id}_X$, $f'=a$, $g=b$, $h=\pr_1$, $e=\pr_2$, and $F=K$, to the diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X&\xleftarrow{\;=\;}&X&\xleftarrow{\;\pr_1\;}&X\times_kY\\
\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle \pr_2}\\
\Spec(k)&\xleftarrow{\;=\;}&\Spec(k)&\xleftarrow{\;b\;}&Y
\end{array}
$$

Both squares are cartesian, since $X\times_k\Spec(k)=X$ and the right square defines $X\times_kY$. The product is finite type over $k$: by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2) the base change $\pr_2:X\times_kY\to Y$ of the finite-type morphism $a$ along $b$ is of finite type, and by clause (1) of the same node the composite $b\circ\pr_2:X\times_kY\to\Spec(k)$ is of finite type. Hence, by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] applied to the affine open $\Spec(k)$, each of $X$ and $X\times_kY$ has a finite affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras. Thus every scheme in the diagram is finite type over $k$, and $n$ is invertible in $k$ as required. The product-square map $\varphi$ specified in [lem-kun-kunneth-via-0f1n] is this specialization of the canonical map of [lem-kun-0f1n], with the displayed constant-complex source. We obtain the isomorphism

$$
\varphi:
E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\underline{\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)}
\longrightarrow
R\pr_{1,*}\bigl(\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr).
$$

source.place: Tag 0F1P (lemma-kunneth), first displayed identification via Tag 0F1N; current blueprint proof paragraph 1

proof.text: Write $W=X\times_kY$. The field $k$ is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. The coordinate rings of the finite affine covers of $X$ and $W$ from Step 1 are therefore Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Applying [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space] to each chart shows that every chart has Noetherian underlying space.

source.place: Tag 0F1P, qcqs hypotheses; algebra.tex Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), affine Noetherian charts

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-finite-union-noetherian] to the finite covers of Step 2: the underlying spaces of $X$ and $W$ are Noetherian. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets], every subset of either underlying space is quasi-compact. In particular, every open subset is quasi-compact, including the whole space and the empty open.

source.place: Tag 0F1P, qcqs hypotheses; topology.tex Tags 0053 (lemma-finite-union-Noetherian) and 04ZA (lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact)

proof.text: By Step 3, $X$ is quasi-compact. Any morphism with source $X$ or $W$ has quasi-compact inverse images of affine opens: those inverse images are open subsets of its source. This is quasi-compactness by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply this observation to $\pr_1:W\to X$ and to both diagonals $W\to W\times_XW$ and $X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$. By [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], $\pr_1$ and $X$ are quasi-separated. Hence $\pr_1$ is qcqs and $X$ is qcqs.

source.place: Tag 0F1P, qcqs checks for Tag 0F12 and unbounded Leray; quasi-compact and quasi-separated definitions

proof.text: The projection $\pr_1$ is a $k$-morphism between the finite-type schemes $W$ and $X$ of Step 1. Consequently [lem-kun-0f10](1) gives $\operatorname{cd}(\pr_1)<\infty$. Since $k$ is separably closed, clause (2) of the same node gives $\operatorname{cd}(X)<\infty$. Its statement already incorporates the separably closed point calculation.

Put $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, $Q=R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},K)$ and $B=\pr_1^{-1}E\otimes^L_\Lambda\pr_2^{-1}K$. Since $n\Lambda=0$, the ring $\Lambda$ is torsion, including when $n=1$. Apply [lem-kun-0f12] with the qcqs scheme $X$ of Step 4, its finite cohomological dimension from Step 5, and the arbitrary unbounded complex $Q\in D(\Lambda)$. Its canonical map $r:R\Gamma(X_{\Et},E)\otimes^L_\Lambda Q\to R\Gamma(X_{\Et},E\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline Q)$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-kun-leray-unbdd], since $\pr_1$ is qcqs by Step 4 and has finite cohomological dimension by Step 5, there is a canonical isomorphism $\ell:R\Gamma(W_{\Et},B)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X_{\Et},R\pr_{1,*}B)$.

source.place: Tag 0F1P, conclusion using Tag 0F12 (lemma-pull-out-constant-mod-n); current blueprint lem-kun-leray-unbdd, statement

proof.text: By the precise map identity in [lem-kun-kunneth-via-0f1n], the Kunneth map of [def-kun-kunneth-map] is $\ell^{-1}\circ R\Gamma(X_{\Et},\varphi)\circ r$, for $\varphi$ from Step 1 and $r,\ell$ from Step 6. A functor preserves inverses by its identity and composition laws, so $R\Gamma(X_{\Et},\varphi)$ is an isomorphism. Explicitly the composite has inverse $r^{-1}\circ R\Gamma(X_{\Et},\varphi^{-1})\circ\ell$. Thus the specified canonical Kunneth map is invertible for all unbounded $E,K$.

source.place: Tag 0F1P, final inference; current blueprint lem-kun-kunneth-via-0f1n, canonical composite identity

theorem isIso_kunnethMap_of_isSepClosed {W : Scheme.{u}} (p₁ : W ⟶ X) (p₂ : W ⟶ Y)
    (sq : IsPullback p₁ p₂ aX aY)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))) :
    IsIso (kunnethMap (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) p₁ p₂ aX aY (p₁ ≫ aX) rfl sq.w.symm E K)
lean.note: The live upstream source explicitly states blueprint thm-kun-0f1p for the same canonical kunnethMap recorded by def-kun-kunneth-map. Specialize its finite coefficient ring Λ to ULift.{u+1} (ZMod n) (the same ring under the canonical ULift ring equivalence, with module carriers in universe u+1); n ≥ 1 makes Λ finite, n annihilates Λ, and IsUnit (n : k) supplies HasInvertibleExponent Λ (Spec (.of k)). LocallyOfFiniteType plus QuasiCompact is exactly finite type. Take W to be the fibre product and sq its IsPullback witness. The conclusion is the node's canonical map in D((Spec k)_et, Λ); the separably closed point equivalence and the canonical Leray and tensor identifications give precisely the displayed map in D(Λ). The adjacent nonempty_iso_kunneth_of_isSepClosed constructs that identification by applying derived global sections to this very map; the attachment uses IsIso of the specified map, not a bare existence of an isomorphism. No duplicate theorem is written. Read using scompile.py --source, since the older local upstream checkout lacks this module.

Let $k$ be a separably closed

$$
\kappa_{E,K}:\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\kunZn}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)
\longrightarrow
\RGamma\bigl((X\times_kY)_{\Et},
\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
By [lem-kun-0f1n] applied to the diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X&\xleftarrow{\;=\;}&X&\xleftarrow{\;\pr_1\;}&X\times_kY\\
\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle \pr_2}\\
\Spec(k)&\longleftarrow&\Spec(k)&\xleftarrow{\;=\;}&Y
\end{array}
$$

(all schemes of finite type over $k$, $n$ invertible in $k$) we
have the isomorphism

$$
\varphi:
E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\underline{\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)}
\longrightarrow
R\pr_{1,*}\bigl(\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr).
$$

We conclude by [lem-kun-kunneth-via-0f1n] and the following
two identifications: first,
$\RGamma((X\times_kY)_{\Et},-)\cong\RGamma(X_{\Et},-)\circ R\pr_{1,*}$
by [lem-kun-leray-unbdd], which applies because $\pr_1$ is a
qcqs morphism of finite type schemes over $k$ and
$\kuncd(\pr_1)<\infty$ by [lem-kun-0f10](1); second,

$$
\RGamma\bigl(X_{\Et},E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\underline{\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)}\bigr)
\cong\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\kunZn}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)
$$

by [lem-kun-0f12], which applies because
$\kuncd(X)<\infty$ by [lem-kun-cd-sep-closed-point] and
[lem-kun-0f10](2). Hence $\kappa_{E,K}$ (the Kunneth map of
[def-kun-kunneth-map]) is an isomorphism, as desired.
